source.name: EYECANDY Visual Technique Library
source.usage: Technique names and visual-language references only. Do not copy or redistribute third-party clips, GIFs, frames, or artwork.

techniques.name: Central Framing
techniques.guidance: Keep the primary subject or product mechanism locked near center while secondary motion creates depth.

techniques.name: Close-Up
techniques.guidance: Open tight on one decisive visual detail, then reveal the larger system.

techniques.name: Dolly
techniques.guidance: Use a controlled push-in or pull-back to create dimensionality without frantic motion.

techniques.name: Dolly Zoom
techniques.guidance: Use sparingly to visualize a sudden change in perceived scale or risk.

techniques.name: Crash Cut
techniques.guidance: Cut abruptly between two strongly contrasting visual states to create a clean attention reset.

techniques.name: Flash Cut
techniques.guidance: Use a very brief insert for one idea or comparison; avoid flashing brightness or eye-strain effects.

techniques.name: Floating UI
techniques.guidance: Layer interface-like objects in depth so the viewer reads a system rather than a static slide.

techniques.name: Fixed Cam
techniques.guidance: Hold the camera stable while the subject changes, making before/after or state transitions easy to compare.

techniques.name: First-Person
techniques.guidance: Stage the scene from the operator's perspective when the viewer should feel the workflow rather than observe it.

techniques.name: Camera Roll
techniques.guidance: Rotate the scene as a transition accent only; do not use repeated rolling motion that harms legibility.

techniques.name: Dutch Angle
techniques.guidance: Introduce a slight tilt to communicate instability, then level the frame when the solution appears.

techniques.name: Fisheye
techniques.guidance: Use only for a deliberate exaggerated hook; avoid on trust-sensitive product explanation scenes.
